incidents.summary: The Dutch Data Protection Authority fined Experian Netherlands €2.7 million for collecting and using personal data without properly informing individuals or obtaining their consent.

sources.title: Experian Fined €2.7m For GDPR Breach in Netherlands - Infosecurity Magazine
sources.quote: Experian Netherlands has been fined €2.7m by the Dutch Data Protection Authority (AP) for breaching the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).

sources.title: Experian Fined €2.7m For GDPR Breach in Netherlands - Infosecurity Magazine
sources.quote: The regulator found that the credit reporting and analytics company collected and used personal data from public and private sources without properly informing individuals or obtaining their consent.

sources.title: Experian Fined €2.7m For GDPR Breach in Netherlands - Infosecurity Magazine
sources.quote: The AP launched its investigation after receiving complaints from consumers who said they faced unusually high deposits or were denied installment plans by service providers.

incidents.summary: Experian Consumer Services agreed to a $650,000 civil penalty and compliance with the CAN-SPAM Act to settle FTC allegations that its marketing emails lacked an opt-out mechanism.

sources.title: FTC lawsuit reminds businesses: CAN-SPAM means CAN’T spam | Consumer Advice
sources.quote: Experian Consumer Services agreed to pay a $650,000 civil penalty and comply with the CAN-SPAM Act to settle an FTC lawsuit.

sources.title: FTC lawsuit reminds businesses: CAN-SPAM means CAN’T spam | Consumer Advice
sources.quote: The FTC says the emails didn’t include a way for people to opt out of getting them, in violation of the CAN-SPAM Act.

incidents.summary: Experian settled Tyreese Learmond’s lawsuit alleging that it charged him $24.99 twice after he cancelled his ExperianCreditWorks subscription.

sources.title: Experian
sources.quote: He alleged that they improperly charged him $24.99 twice after he cancelled his ExperianCreditWorks membership subscription.

sources.title: Experian
sources.quote: Experian and Learmond settled out of court before trial, formally releasing them from the case while Fidelity remained in the case hoping to compel arbitration under the Federal Arbitration Act.
